item.title: China-Pakistan drill features Type 08 IFV with roof cage, grilles
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21 22:36:00
A Type 08 infantry fighting vehicle fitted with a roof cage and side grilles drives down a road during the China-Pakistan Karakoram 2026 joint army training in Korla, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. Photo: Screenshot from the CCTV News The ongoing China-Pakistan Karakoram 2026 joint army training exercise in Korla, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, has moved into its segmented drill phase, with mixed units completing a full reconnaissance, strike and clearance sequence, CCTV News reported on Wednesday. Highlights of the report include footage of a Chinese Type 08 infantry fighting vehicle (IFV) fitted with a roof cage and side grilles, alongside drone swarms and robot dogs deployed in live drills. A Chinese expert said such adaptations reflect lessons drawn from real combat. Over the past few days, Chinese and Pakistani troops have moved into the segmented phase, which involves missions ranging from air-ground reconnaissance and concentrated fire strikes to search and clearance, with mixed units completing multiple tactical actions and honing joint counter-terrorism skills, reported CCTV. At the start of the drill, reconnaissance vehicles and drones deployed simultaneously to monitor targets inside the camp, tracking the terrorists' force disposition and movements in real time. Once intelligence was gathered, the fire strike phase began immediately. Snipers seized vantage points for long-range kills. Drone swarms launched suicide strikes on exposed targets, while ground armor fire followed to ensure full coverage. The Type 08 IFV then carried the assault team forward, a signal that the fire strike phase had ended, said CCTV. Notably, the vehicle's roof was fitted with a metal grille, with grilles also added to its sides, specifically designed to counter drone attacks. The roof cage on the Type 08 is a rapid tactical adaptation to drone threats, Song Zhongping, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Wednesday. The Russia-Ukraine and Middle East conflicts have shown militaries worldwide just how serious that threat has become. Adding roof protection to armored vehicles is a direct response, drawing on battlefield lessons to improve equipment performance. According to Military Watch Magazine on September 12, the Russia-Ukraine conflict has substantially altered the configuration of Russian tanks. First-person view drones and other unmanned systems have made the upper surfaces, rear sections and engine compartments of tanks particularly vulnerable, with vehicles having consequently appeared with increasingly elaborate roof protection, additional armor and electronic warfare equipment intended to interfere with drone attacks. Earlier, in November 2025, the Xinhua News Agency cited a report from German news channel n-tv that said to better protect vehicles from suicide drone attacks, Russian forces have continued to develop new countermeasures. After the introduction of improvised "turtle shell" and "porcupine" armor, photos of a novel device have circulated on social media, with military bloggers calling it the "hedgehog tank" based on its appearance. Returning to the China-Pakistan drill, CCTV reported that once the IFV reached its position, assault troops dismounted immediately and moved into the terrorist camp, followed by several more Type 08s carrying clearance teams. As soon as they stopped, the troops dismounted. Their mission is to push deeper into the camp to eliminate remaining terrorists. These troops coordinated with robot dogs, which scouted building interiors ahead of them, reducing the risk of casualties. Song noted that this joint training exercise is themed on joint counter-terrorism and clearance operations in high-altitude areas. However, even during counter-terrorism drills, plateau units make full use of asymmetric assets like drones. Terrorist groups also might use drones for sabotage operations, and the PLA must have sufficient means to counter the threat and challenges posed by these drones. In high-altitude environments, drones and counter-drone tactics might see new approaches, and a set of drone and counter-drone tactics suited to plateau terrain needs to be developed. Realistic drills are essential to solidifying tactics and training, Song said. The report noted that despite the language barrier, days of continuous skill training have built tactical chemistry among the mixed teams. "What impressed me most about this joint training is that the Pakistani military has real combat experience, so many of their lessons are worth learning. When we enter a building and throw a grenade, we throw it far; they throw it at the ground so it bounces at speed, ricocheting two or three times instead of staying in one place. That effectively stops the enemy from picking it up and throwing it back," Pan Li, a member of a unit under the Xinjiang military command, was quoted by CCTV as saying. Through days of training, the two sides have learned from each other's tactics, shared combat experience and further refined their skills, effectively improving joint counter-terrorism capabilities, the report said. On October 10, Senior Colonel Chen Xi, a spokesperson for the Chinese Ministry of National Defense, announced that in mid and late October, Chinese and Pakistani armies will hold Karakoram 2026 joint army training in Korla, Xinjiang region. Focusing on joint counter-terrorism operations in high-altitude areas, the activity will include skill training in UAV operation, on-the-move target search and firing, and long-range sniping, as well as cover joint command and live-force exercises. This is the first joint army training to be carried out by the two countries, which will help the two sides deepen cooperation and strengthen interoperability in counter-terrorism. On October 14, CCTV Military channel emphasized in a report that all weapons and equipment were provided by China, including Type 191 rifles, Type 201 squad machine guns, Type 11 armored assault vehicles, Type 08 infantry fighting vehicles, as well as artillery, unmanned and anti-unmanned systems.

item.title: China permits, monitors Philippine resupply to illegally grounded vessel at Ren'ai Jiao: CCG spokesperson
item.description:

File photo of a China Coast Guard (CCG) ship in the South China Sea Photo: VCG With approval from the Chinese side, the Philippines delivered living necessities to its ship illegally "grounded" at China's Ren'ai Jiao on Wednesday, China Coast Guard (CCG) spokesperson Jiang Lue said, according to a statement from the CCG on Wednesday. Global Times

item.title: Chinese expert calls Japan's six reports on PLA activities over two days sensationalism aimed at justifying own military buildup
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20 22:31:00
The Type 901 sea-going comprehensive replenishment ship Hulunhu (Hull 901) conducts an underway replenishment drill. Photo: China Military Online Japan's Defense Ministry issued six consecutive reports on Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) ship and aircraft movements on Monday and Tuesday, covering the 48th escort task group, a supply ship, electronic reconnaissance vessels and reconnaissance aircraft. A military expert said that, with the Liaoning carrier group training in the far seas and the large US-Japan "Keen Sword 27" exercise underway, the frequent disclosures amount to alarmism aimed at justifying Japan's military buildup. On Tuesday, the ministry claimed the PLA Navy's Type 054A guided-missile frigate Jingzhou (Hull 532) had transited the Osumi Strait toward the Pacific on Monday. Monday's five reports included one claiming that on Saturday, the PLA Navy's Type 052D destroyer Tangshan (Hull 122), Type 054A frigate Daqing (Hull 576) and Type 903A comprehensive supply ship Taihu (Hull 889) passed through the Miyako Strait into the East China Sea. These vessels make up the PLA 48th escort task group, which set sail on October 11, 2025, and handed over duties to the 49th task force on September 7, according to reports from state media outlets. The group has not yet returned home, meaning the deployment has now exceeded a year. The Japanese ministry also claimed on Monday that the Type 052D destroyer Qiqihar (Hull 121) and the Type 901 sea-going comprehensive replenishment ship Hulunhu (Hull 901) transited the Osumi Strait into the Western Pacific on Saturday. Two other notices claimed the PLA Navy's electronic reconnaissance ship 796 entered the Western Pacific through the Miyako Strait on Saturday, while electronic reconnaissance ship 798 passed through the Osumi Strait into the Western Pacific between Saturday and Sunday. A fifth notice said that on Monday, a PLA BZK-005 reconnaissance drone and a Y-9 intelligence-gathering aircraft flew from the East China Sea through the Miyako Strait into the Pacific, circled over the ocean and returned. The same day, a PLA TB-001 reconnaissance/strike drone flew from the East China Sea through the area between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan island into the Pacific. Zhang Junshe, a Chinese military affairs expert, offered his analysis of the reports. The Hulunhu is a new-generation comprehensive supply ship independently developed by China to world-class standards, capable of providing underway replenishment for carrier groups and far-sea maneuver formations, Zhang told the Global Times. A carrier group typically consists of an aircraft carrier, destroyers, frigates, logistics support ships and a nuclear submarine. Japan had already released reports on two Type 055 destroyers and a Type 052D, and has now added a large comprehensive supply ship. This likely means the Hulunhu could subsequently join the Liaoning carrier group conducting far-sea training in the Western Pacific. The PLA Navy sent the Liaoning carrier task group to the Western Pacific on October 14 for training, the PLA Navy said in a statement. This is the Liaoning 's second far-sea training deployment to the Western Pacific this year, which also marks the 10th anniversary of its first such deployment in late December 2016, more than four years after the carrier entered service. The Hulunhu can quickly conduct both alongside and vertical replenishment of large volumes of supplies with high efficiency, supporting carrier operations far from shore. If it joined the Liaoning group, the formation would gain sustained training and extended far-sea presence without port calls, enabling longer exercises and more complex drills, and improving the carrier group's ocean-going endurance, presence and combat capability, Zhang said. Meanwhile, a large US-Japan exercise is currently underway. The US and Japan were set to launch the large-scale "Keen Sword 27" military exercise, involving more than 50,000 personnel from the SDF and US forces, on Monday, the Kyodo News reported on Saturday. Against the backdrop of the Liaoning 's far-sea training and the US-Japan drills, Zhang said, the Chinese reconnaissance aircraft and ships could provide situational awareness and intelligence support for the carrier group to a certain extent. This multi-layered reconnaissance setup reflects the PLA Navy's approach to system-based far-sea training and joint operations. First, it builds a far-sea comprehensive support and situational awareness system, improving the carrier group's sustained combat capability and information advantage in complex waters far from base. Second, complementary reconnaissance platforms enable three-dimensional, real-time battlefield awareness, improving information acquisition and responsiveness in complex electromagnetic environments and high-intensity confrontations. Third, it tests and improves system-based combat effectiveness in realistic conditions, reflecting a combat-oriented training approach, the expert explained. Zhang noted Japan's frequent releases of PLA ship and aircraft movements, sometimes multiple notices in a single day, amount to making a fuss out of nothing. During past training, Chinese naval formations have consistently handled tracking, surveillance and harassment by foreign parties, especially Japan, in accordance with laws and regulations. The Western Pacific is not any country's backyard, and international waterways are not anyone's doorstep. Additionally, Japan's sensationalism cannot hinder the normal development of China's national defense, Zhang added.

item.title: Chinese PLA forces track, monitor USS Charleston after illegal intrusion into waters adjacent to China's Xianbin Jiao
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20 13:32:00
This photo carried in a report named "A Survey Report on the Coral Reef Ecosystem of Xianbin Jiao" shows an aerial view of Xianbin Jiao of China's Nansha Qundao. Photo: Xinhua In the early hours of Tuesday, the US littoral combat ship USS Charleston illegally intruded into the waters adjacent to Xianbin Jiao of China's Nansha Qundao without approval from the Chinese government. The People's Liberation Army (PLA) Southern Theater Command Navy dispatched forces to track and monitor the US vessel in accordance with laws and regulations, Yin Gang, a spokesperson for the PLA Southern Theater Command Navy, said in a statement on Tuesday. China holds indisputable sovereignty over Nansha Qundao and its adjacent waters. The US action infringes upon China's sovereign rights and interests, jeopardizes maritime security, and is detrimental to regional peace and stability. The US side should immediately cease such activities, Yin said. Forces of the Southern Theater Command remain on high alert at all times to resolutely safeguard national sovereignty and security and uphold regional peace and stability, said the spokesperson. Xianbin Jiao lies in the southeastern waters of China's Nansha Qundao, and its position along several international shipping lanes gives it significant strategic importance. The US littoral combat ship's close-in provocation there is a calculated move driven by the area's geostrategic value and other considerations, Zhang Junshe, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Tuesday. Through such calculated provocations, the US seeks to test China's red lines on maritime passage and regional control while obstructing China's law enforcement and sovereignty protection efforts around the shoal. This deliberately challenges China's sovereignty in the South China Sea and undermines regional peace under the guise of so-called "freedom of navigation," said Zhang. Compared with previous US military operations conducted under the banner of "freedom of navigation," those near Xianbin Jiao have been relatively rare. Yet this latest move suggests that US policy toward the South China Sea remains fundamentally unchanged and that China-US competition in these waters continues. The operation also aims to signal support for the Philippines and underscore the US military presence in the South China Sea, Chen Xiangmiao, a research fellow at the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, told the Global Times. Xianbin Jiao has been a flashpoint in China Philippines maritime frictions in recent years. For example, in September, a Philippine vessel caused a collision with a China Coast Guard (CCG) boat near Xianbin Jiao in China's Nansha Qundao after ignoring repeated warnings and cutting across its bow, Jiang Lue, a spokesperson for the CCG, said in a statement. Jiang also sternly warned the Philippine side to immediately stop all acts of infringement and provocation, or bear all consequences arising from them. Zhang noted that Philippine coast guard vessels have repeatedly intruded illegally into waters around Xianbin Jiao and staged beaching provocations, seeking to create a fact on the ground to assert Manila's so-called "sovereignty." By dispatching warships for close-in provocations at this juncture, the US also aims to provide military backing for Manila's risky moves, tie down China's navy and coast guard, and raise China's maritime governance costs while maximizing disruption at minimal cost. China's swift public response to the US littoral combat ship's incursion into waters around Xianbin Jiao underscores its resolve to defend national sovereignty, territorial integrity, and maritime rights and interests. It also demonstrates the Chinese military's vigilance and readiness to counter security threats, sending a clear message: China will brook no compromise on these core interests, said Zhang. The prompt official statement following the early-morning incident highlights China's round-the-clock surveillance and rapid-response capabilities in the South China Sea. "Unauthorized intrusions that infringe upon China's rights can be detected, tracked and addressed without delay," said the expert.

item.title: State media explains modular refueling pods' role in Y-20B dual tanker-transport capability
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19 19:45:00
A Y-20B large transport aircraft sits with its cargo hold open for loading. Photo: Screenshot from the CCTV News CCTV News reported on Monday on a recently circulated image of the Y-20B large transport aircraft that shows refueling pods mounted under the wings while its cargo hold is open for loading. Military affairs experts in the report analyzed the Y-20B's dual transport-refueling configuration and what makes it so capable. The image was first published by the PLA Daily on Wednesday. According to the CCTV report, the Y-20 family has grown steadily in recent years. The Y-20A focuses on strategic airlifts, the YU-20 on aerial refueling, and the domestically developed Y-20B - built on the same platform as the Y-20A but with a new-generation power system - is a modular design that can handle both cargo transport and aerial refueling. How does a transport aircraft carry out refueling missions? Military commentator Fu Qianshao explained that the Y-20B's refueling pods are modular and detachable, allowing the aircraft to switch roles at any time depending on the mission. Fu told the CCTV that pod placement is critical. If mounted too far outboard, wingtip vortices can interfere with the refueling hoses; if too far inboard, two fighters being refueled simultaneously would be too close together, creating potential danger. Thanks to testing with the YU-20, the Y-20B requires no major structural changes, making conversion relatively simple. In the published image, the Y-20B has refueling pods under its wings while its cargo hold remains empty, preserving full transport space. This means the aircraft relies on its own internal fuel to provide limited refueling support through the pods. "The Y-20B's internal fuel capacity is already very large, so no additional tanks are needed to refuel heavy or medium fighters. Tests have shown that without extra tanks, the aircraft is lighter and thus burns less fuel, so its refueling output is not significantly affected," Fu was quoted by CCTV as saying. The report noted that the PLA Air Force has fielded heavy transport aircraft and tankers in recent years, and the Y-20B's dual-role capability offers new flexibility. Fu said that developing and producing dedicated tankers would tie up part of the transport fleet. However, with this modification, a large number of Y-20Bs could be deployed on a given strategic axis to temporarily handle refueling during long-range strike missions, and while refueling, they can still carry cargo, personnel and other supplies. CCTV also noted that multi-role capability may be a future trend. Previously, a documentary on the domestically developed Y-20 family aired by state media on August 5 revealed that a pilot said the Y-20B could take on roles including bomber, early warning aircraft and electronic warfare platform. Song Zhongping, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times that by equipping different functional pods, the aircraft can quickly change roles: with refueling pods, it becomes a tanker; with electronic jamming pods, an electronic warfare platform; with bombing modules, it could potentially perform bombing missions; and with early warning modules, it can serve as an airborne early warning platform. Thanks to the Y-20's fully indigenous design, Song said, Chinese engineers have a comprehensive understanding of its aerodynamic configuration, airframe structure, flight control and avionics systems. This means that, as long as technical conditions are met, modifications can be carried out with greater flexibility and tailored to operational needs. The Y-20B's multi-role capability greatly enhances the PLA Air Force's mission flexibility and support efficiency. Military commentator Song Xiaojun told the CCTV that the Y-20 platform's conversion potential could extend to drone operations. "For example, a large transport aircraft could carry swarms of small drones and release them at a distance from the battlefield, effectively becoming an 'airborne drone carrier.' And as a tanker, could it refuel drones? In the future, aerial refueling between drones and crewed aircraft is entirely possible," Song Xiaojun was quoted by CCTV as saying. On July 6, 2016, the Y-20 officially entered service with PLA Air Force aviation units. A decade later, the Y-20 has evolved from a single transport platform into a family of models including the Y-20A, Y-20B and YU-20 aerial refueling tanker, with its operations extending to more than 40 countries and regions across four continents, according to the Aviation Industry Corporation of China, the aircraft's manufacturer, on its WeChat account in June.

item.title: Four of the PLA Navy's Type 071 amphibious dock landing ships conduct rare live-fire exercise: state media report
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18 21:13:00
A scene of the live-fire drill Photo: WeChat account of the PLA Southern Theater Command State broadcaster CCTV News reported on Saturday on a rare live-fire drill involving four of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy's Type 071 amphibious dock landing ships. A Chinese military expert said the training could have involved a complex training simulation calling for multi-type landing ships to train together to prepare for island-reef assault, transportation and sovereignty defense missions in locations such as the South China Sea and the Taiwan Straits. According to the CCTV footage, a naval flotilla under the Southern Theater Command recently organized a task group for multi-subject combat-oriented training at sea. Footage showed the Type 071 landing ships Kunlunshan (Hull 998) and Changbaishan (Hull 989) sailing side by side. The PLA Southern Theater Command's WeChat account said on Friday that the four Type 071 ships also included the Qilianshan (Hull 985) and Wuzhishan (Hull 987). During one maneuver, combat alerts suddenly sounded. The ships quickly changed formation as orders came down from the combat command rooms and all stations coordinated closely together. Radar stations locked onto incoming targets, and the formation gave the order to engage. Main and secondary guns opened fire in succession, completing air-defense interception strikes. Image of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy's Type 071 amphibious dock landing ships Kunlunshan (Hull 998) and Changbaishan (Hull 989) Photo: WeChat account of the PLA Southern Theater Command Between missions, simulated replenishment training was carried out. Ships quickly took up replenishment positions, prepared equipment and fired line-throwing devices, with officers and soldiers working in close coordination throughout. The training closely followed real combat requirements, setting up realistic battlefield conditions to sharpen the formation's emergency response capabilities in complex sea and air conditions, the Southern Theater Command said. The nearly 20,000-ton Type 071 ship is currently one of the PLA's main amphibious warfare assets. Its primary mission is to deliver amphibious vehicles, landing craft or air-cushioned landing craft to the optimal distance from the shoreline, and to serve as a temporary base for assaulting beaches, resupplying ammunition and provisions, and acting as a field hospital, according to CCTV's military channel. Wang Yunfei, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Sunday that the Type 071 is the PLA Navy's main amphibious landing ship, primarily transporting tanks, armored vehicles and other equipment, and exists in large numbers across the fleet. These ships can carry a reinforced battalion, enough to handle general escort and offensive-defensive operations, and can also carry shipborne helicopters for vertical landings, making them a relatively comprehensive landing ship with three-dimensional attack and defense capabilities. Wang said that in potential combat scenarios in the South China Sea and Taiwan Straits, the focus is on island and reef assault, transport and sovereignty defense. Considering the current complex nature of the South China Sea situation, training multiple landing ship types together takes into account potential future operations, he noted. According to a caption of one of the images published by China Military Online on July 27, the Changbaishan , attached to a naval flotilla under the PLA Southern Theater Command, conducted joint operations in coordination with Z-20J shipborne helicopters and a landing craft air cushion during a multi-subject maritime training exercise in mid to late July. In the future, the Type 071 can form even larger landing formations with the Type 075 and Type 076 amphibious assault ships, Wang noted. The Type 075 ship focuses on vertical landings and carrying more helicopters, the Type 076 can carry more drones, while the Type 071 might mainly carry amphibious tanks and armored vehicles, making the three tactically complementary. Previously, CCTV reports on July 24 and 25 noted that two videos circulating online had drawn public attention. The footage in these videos shows naval Z-20J helicopters appearing on the decks of the Type 075 amphibious assault ships Hainan and Hubei . Notably, the Z-20J aboard the Hubei recently accompanied the carrier ship to a training area in the South China Sea for multi-subject combat-oriented drills. This public display sends a clear signal that the new-generation utility helicopter is being integrated into the core configuration of the PLA Navy's amphibious operations. With the shipborne version of the Z-20 helicopter having takeoff and landing capabilities on Type 075 amphibious assault ships, China's amphibious warfare system has undergone a critical upgrade, CCTV said.

item.title: AVIC Chengdu adopts 'LEGO-style' modular tooling design, cuts aircraft manufacturing costs
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16 12:28:00
Photo: Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC)'s Weibo account Chengdu Aircraft Corporation (CAC) under Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC) - the manufacturer of China's J-20 and J-10 fighter series, has adopted a "LEGO-style" modular design approach to aircraft tooling, allowing standardized components to be rapidly assembled and reused across different projects, cutting direct costs by more than 20 percent in some research tasks. Building an aircraft requires not only the aircraft itself, but also numerous "unsung heroes" behind the scenes - process equipment collectively known as tooling. As a critical part of aircraft manufacturing, the development speed and cost of tooling directly affect an aircraft's production cycle and manufacturing costs, according to a release from the AVIC's official Weibo account on Thursday. Starting at the design stage, CAC has moved away from the traditional model of developing customized tooling for individual aircraft types. Instead, it has adopted a development approach centered on standardized design and shared modular components, while promoting unified tooling design. The tooling is built from standardized modules that can be quickly configured and reused for different requirements, much like LEGO building blocks. The R&D team launched a technical research program covering five key categories of tooling: assembly tooling, work platforms, transport vehicles, support frames and lifting rigs. Common structures were standardized into 163 shared basic modules, raising the overall modular reuse rate to more than 80 percent. These standard modules can be selected and assembled as needed, enabling rapid reconfiguration and reuse across different tasks and components, according to the release. CAC is widely known for being the manufacturer of China's premier fighter aircraft, including the J-20 stealth fighter jet and the J-10 fighter series. This "LEGO-style" modular tooling model can significantly improve design and production efficiency while substantially reducing manufacturing costs. Its advantages are particularly evident in scenarios that require rapid expansion of production capacity, Wang Ya'nan, chief editor of Aerospace Knowledge magazine, told the Global Times on Friday. Traditionally, different types of aircraft required dedicated tooling because of variations in size, structure, materials, assembly methods and production processes. Each new aircraft therefore needed a complete set of custom-built tooling, from small jigs and templates to large transport platforms. Once production ended, much of that tooling had to be stored or scrapped because it could not be reused for other models. Developing a new tooling system also required dedicated design, R&D and production teams, making the process lengthy and costly, said Wang. CAC has introduced a unified modular design approach for tooling, centered on standardization. Many tooling components can be shared across different aircraft models, with only the adapter sections that directly interface with the aircraft requiring modification. Proven modules can be combined with newly designed model-specific parts, avoiding the need to develop an entire tooling system from scratch. This approach shortens development cycles, cuts costs and reduces tooling design complexity, according to the expert. The AVIC release also noted that the full implementation of unified-type design has yielded tangible results. Tooling development costs have been reduced by about 20 percent, while development cycles have been shortened by roughly 25 percent. Modular coverage has reached 80 percent for reconfigurable flexible assembly tooling and 90 percent for work platforms. The unified-type application rates for transport vehicles, support frames and lifting rigs have reached 84 percent, 60 percent and 87 percent, respectively. In certain research projects, tooling can be reused across multiple aircraft, significantly reducing the amortized cost per airframe and delivering direct cost savings of more than 20 percent. The approach has helped address the long-standing challenge of high tooling costs and provides a replicable and scalable model for low-cost development in the aviation process equipment sector, according to the release. Wang noted that the successful implementation of this approach suggests that CAC has thoroughly assessed its current and near-term production equipment needs, with advance planning and preparations in place for short-notice and large-scale production demands.

item.title: Philippine military backs suspension of direct communication with China, raising risks of misjudgment, escalation: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14 22:02:00
Defense Secretary of the Philippines Gilbert Teodoro Jr. File photo: VCG The Philippine military has thrown its support behind Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr.'s suspension of direct military-to-military communication channels with China, as the Chinese Embassy in Manila warned that shutting down such contact fuels mistrust and narrows the space for crisis management amid continuing tensions in the South China Sea. The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) claimed Tuesday that it "stands solidly behind and firmly supports" Teodoro's move, according to a report from the Philippine News Agency on Tuesday. A Chinese expert noted that the suspension of military-to-military communications between China and the Philippines would further undermine dialogue and mutual trust, while increasing the risk of misjudging each other's intentions. In the context of frequent maritime encounters, such miscalculations could severely weaken crisis management, raise the likelihood of sudden or unintended incidents, and expose frontline personnel on both sides to greater risks if tensions escalate unexpectedly because of less available communication channels. The AFP spokesperson, retired Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, claimed communication mechanisms could only work when based on what he described as mutual trust, sincerity and support for international law. He claimed bilateral dialogue had failed because "the messages" did not match "the actions on sea, air and ground," and accused China of using direct communication as a "smokescreen," a report in the Philippine Star said on Wednesday. Trinidad also claimed that the AFP will continue to perform its sea patrol and "will keep performing rotation and resupply missions," according to the Philippine Star report. The Chinese Embassy in the Philippines, responding to the suspension, said "communication channels should remain open to avoid miscalculation and prevent tensions from escalating." The Embassy criticized Teodoro for shutting down military-to-military communication for "political self interests," warning that the move "fuels mistrust, narrows the space for crisis management, and pushes frontline personnel closer to confrontation," according to the Embassy's Facebook account. The current dispute indicates that the suspension did not begin this week. Coverage from Philippine-based media outlet the Daily Tribune said that Teodoro claimed on Tuesday that military-to-military communication with China had been suspended for nearly three years. In a May 2024 statement posted by the Philippine Department of National Defense, Teodoro said he had disallowed contact between the department and the Chinese Embassy since a courtesy call by then Chinese Ambassador Huang Xilian shortly after Teodoro took office in July 2023. Although China and the Philippines maintain other communication channels, they cannot fully replace direct military-to-military contact. Diplomatic channels are mainly used for broader policy and strategic coordination, while coast guard communication focuses more on specific maritime law enforcement. Military exchanges, by contrast, deal with more specialized and sensitive issues involving defense policy, military strategy and security concerns, Chen Xiangmiao, a research fellow at the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, told the Global Times on Wednesday. Chen noted that military communication serves as an important "backstop" for bilateral relations. Even when serious differences exist in the South China Sea, direct military contact can help clarify strategic intentions and security red lines, preventing specific maritime incidents from escalating into broader military confrontations. Given that the Philippine military also plays a role in planning and directing some maritime operations, restoring effective military-to-military communication remains important if Manila genuinely wants to manage disputes and reduce risks, Chen said. The latest military position comes as the Marcos administration stresses that the president intends to maintain engagement with Beijing. Palace communications undersecretary Claire Castro said that Manila would continue engaging with China, particularly in trade and investment, a report from News Watch Plus Philippines on Tuesday shows. Just days earlier, Marcos said his "greatest fear" was that a mistake by a seaman or soldier could develop into "something that goes out of control," while stressing the importance of managing problems and preventing misunderstandings in the South China Sea. The expert pointed out that the Philippine government's position appears to be internally inconsistent: while the presidential palace stresses dialogue and maintaining normal engagement with China, the defense establishment supports suspending direct military communication. Cutting such a channel would not make the Philippines safer, but would further weaken trust, increase the risk of miscalculation and ultimately impose greater security and political costs on Manila. Chen said this reflects a "double-track" approach: Manila portrays itself as willing to communicate and maintain overall bilateral stability, while continuing actions in the South China Sea that undermine existing understandings and create new friction. If the Philippines genuinely wants to manage risks, it should stop provocative actions, return to dialogue and restore effective crisis-management channels, including military-to-military communication.

item.title: First China-Pakistan army joint training features an all-Chinese equipment lineup, signaling deep interoperability: expert

Published: 2026-10-14 21:19:00
Image of the opening ceremony of the China-Pakistan Karakoram 2026 joint army training held at a training base in Korla, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Photo: Screenshot from the CCTV's military channel The first China-Pakistan army joint training Karakoram 2026 kicked off on Wednesday, with all weapons and equipment provided by the Chinese side, China Central Television's (CCTV) military channel reported. A military affairs expert said the choice of medium-weight wheeled vehicles for high-altitude operations, and Pakistan's use of an all-Chinese lineup, signal deepening military trust and potential future procurement. The opening ceremony for the China-Pakistan Karakoram 2026 joint army training was held at a training base in Korla, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. It is the first army joint training between the two countries, themed on joint counter-terrorism and clearance operations in high-altitude areas, said the report. The report said that all weapons and equipment in the training were provided by China, including Type 191 rifles, Type 201 squad machine guns, Type 11 armored assault vehicles, Type 08 infantry fighting vehicles, as well as artillery, unmanned and anti-unmanned systems. Wang Yunfei, a military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Wednesday that the two types of vehicles are both wheeled platforms. In high-altitude areas, wheeled armored vehicles have their own advantages. Unlike tracked vehicles, they are faster, especially during road maneuvers, and easier to maintain, making them well-suited for movement and combat missions on the plateau. The all-Chinese equipment lineup covers multiple categories and forms a relatively complete combat system, he said. On one hand, it shows China has provided weapons and equipment technology to Pakistan. On the other hand, these weapons could be procured by Pakistan in future military trade, further expanding the presence of Chinese equipment in the Pakistan Army. This joint training thus serves as a rehearsal and a process of familiarization. From a broader perspective, it also reflects strategic mutual trust, showing that military cooperation between the two countries has reached a high level. Building this kind of deep interoperability will lay a solid foundation for future joint operations between the two armies in counter-terrorism, border control and other areas, the expert said. Zhang Jueshe, another military affairs expert, told the Global Times that China and Pakistan complement each other well in the field of counter-terrorism, while cooperation can be advanced via intelligence sharing, joint operations, technology transfers, experience exchanges and economic cooperation. "China could provide Pakistan with technical and equipment support, including drones and smart combat platforms, to boost its surveillance and early warning capacity against terrorist groups, and also conduct experience training," he noted. Pakistan's experience in addressing complex border security situations, handling local separatist forces and coordinating counter-terrorism efforts can also provide references for China to tackle similar non-traditional security challenges, Zhang added. On Saturday, Senior Colonel Chen Xi, a spokesperson for the Chinese Ministry of National Defense, announced that in mid- and late October, Chinese and Pakistani armies will hold Karakoram 2026 joint army training in Korla, Xinjiang. Focusing on joint counter-terrorism operations in high-altitude areas, the activity will include skills training in UAV operation, on-the-move target search and firing, and long-range sniping, and cover joint command and live-force exercises. The exercise will expand the scope of China-Pakistan military cooperation, reflect growing mutual trust, and strengthen counter-terrorism collaboration through the sharing of experience and expertise, Zhang said.
